title: Spotting the error in a solution graph

stem.text: Use the data display together with the information in the question.

prompt.text: Arif solved 19-3x>10 and drew the number line shown. Enter 1 if it is correct, 2 if only the circle at the boundary is wrong, 3 if only the direction of the solution line is wrong, or 4 if both are wrong.

content.text: Solve the inequality yourself first. Think about what dividing by a negative number does to the sign.
Subtract 19 from both sides, divide both sides by -3, then compare your solution with the drawing.
Dividing by -3 reverses the sign, so the correct solution has an open circle at 3 and a line going left.
The drawing has the correct open circle but its line goes right, so only the direction is wrong: code 3.
